brandingHint: Only platform administrators can change platform configuration. Saving a deployment domain immediately updates public URLs such as the MCP endpoint and Executor startup commands. Without a domain, the deployment environment URL is used.
domainHint: Enter the URL users visit for this deployment, for example https://wonder.example.com. Saving it immediately updates public URLs such as the MCP endpoint and Executor startup commands.
logoTooLarge: Logo files must not exceed 512 KB
logoHint: Supports PNG, JPG/JPEG, WebP, SVG, GIF, ICO and AVIF, up to 512 KB.
accentHint: The accent color applies to primary buttons, links, selections and focus indicators. Page backgrounds and success, warning and error colors stay the same.
primaryColorHint: Use the color control on the left or enter a #RRGGBB value to customize the primary color. Click Save configuration to apply your changes.
imLoadFailed: Failed to load collaboration notification configuration
wecomConnectionSeparate: Save success and connection success are shown separately
wecomNotReadyDisabled: The WeCom channel is not enabled
wecomReadyHint: Configuration is saved and the long connection is established.
providerHint: Choose Feishu, DingTalk or WeCom for the platform. Project notifications and personal IM identities follow this setting.
channelHint: After switching and saving, the previous channel stops sending notifications.
keepSecretHint: Leave blank to keep the configured AppSecret
keepSecret: Leave blank to keep the current secret
notificationSectionHint: System notifications are sent to users. Notification and group-chat configurations are saved separately.
groupChatSectionHint: Used by Workspaces to bind groups and talk to Agents. Workspace admins still need to provide the group ID and the Agent.
currentChannelHint: Notification delivery and group-chat access in every Workspace follow this setting.
switchChannelBody: This affects platform-wide notifications and group-chat access in every Workspace. The previous channel stops sending notifications and receiving new messages while accepted messages finish processing; existing bindings and app configuration are kept and resume when you switch back. Switching does not enable the target channel; its notification and group-chat bots still need to be configured and enabled separately.
switchChannelDirty: You have unsaved changes. Confirming the switch explicitly discards the current notification and group-chat drafts; this warning does not block the switch.
imSwitchHint: After switching, the previous channel stops receiving new messages while accepted messages finish processing. Shared group-chat bindings can only be created on the current channel.
groupChatSaveFailed: Failed to save group-chat bot configuration
groupChatLoadFailed: Failed to load group-chat bot configuration
groupChatStatusHint: This is the state the platform configuration permits. It does not mean every group is bound and usable, nor that every message is processed or delivered successfully.
groupChatSetupHint: Configure the {{provider}} platform shared group-chat bot. Workspace administrators only need a group ID and an Agent to create a binding.
groupChatDescription: Notifications and group chats can use the same application or separate applications. Each scenario is saved and enabled independently. To share an application, enter the same application identity and credentials in both sections.
feishuBaseUrlHint: Leave blank to use the official address https://open.feishu.cn/open-apis; for a self-hosted gateway, enter the full address including any path prefix.
keepToken: Leave blank to keep the existing Token
tokenHelp: Find this under “Events & callbacks → Encryption strategy” in the Feishu app
keepEncryption: Encryption is configured; leave blank to keep the existing key
encryptionHelp: Optional. Match the Feishu encryption strategy.
clearEncryption: Clear Encrypt Key (also disable encryption in Feishu)
adminPermission: Only platform administrators can perform this action
adminHint: Platform administrators manage platform configuration, collaboration notifications and all Workspaces, including the recycle bin. Administrators cannot remove themselves, and at least one must remain.
searchHint: Search by name, username or email
selfRemoval: You cannot remove yourself as a platform administrator
lastAdmin: At least one platform administrator must remain
ssoHint: Enterprise SSO is visible and editable to platform administrators only; the API still checks permissions. When no connection is enabled, the login page shows the AutoWonder account sign-in only.
ssoIdpDescriptionPlaceholder: Identifies this identity source in the platform; optional
ssoDisableIdpImpact: {{connections}} login connections under this identity provider will stop working and their entries are removed from the login page.
ssoIdpDisableHint: Disabling an identity provider stops all of its login connections; re-enabling it does not restore the previous default sign-in setting.
ssoConnectionHint: A connection is one entry on the login page. At most one default sign-in exists platform-wide; the login page starts its authentication automatically.
ssoConnectionNameHint: This name appears on the login page button, for example “Sign in with Employee SSO”.
ssoConnectionDisableHint: Disabling a connection or its identity provider removes the entry; the default sign-in switch works only when both the connection and its identity provider are enabled.
ssoSamlCallbackHint: SAML 2.0: enter this address as the IdP ACS / reply URL and ensure the assertion audience matches the issuer.
ssoOidcCallbackHint: OIDC: enter this address as the application redirect URI.
ssoCallbackDeployHint: The address uses the platform deployment public address, not the current browser origin. Update it after changing the domain.
ssoSamlCertHint: Used to verify SAML response signatures; complete the certificate rotation on the IdP before replacing it.
ssoClientSecretKeepHint: Only a “configured” marker is shown; the stored secret is never echoed back.
ssoClientSecretPlaceholder: Leave blank to keep the configured secret
ssoAttributeHint: Field names come from IdP assertion attributes; protocol defaults apply when left blank.
ssoAllowedTenantsHint: Separate multiple values with commas; validated against the ID token tenant claim, and only listed tenants can sign in.
ssoEnableConnectionHint: When disabled, the login page no longer shows this entry; existing sessions are unaffected.
ssoNewConnectionDisabledHint: New connections start disabled. Enable one after confirming its configuration.
ssoEditLockedHint: When editing, the identity provider and protocol are locked; saved values such as the client secret are never echoed back.
ssoLoadFailed: Failed to load enterprise SSO configuration
ssoEmptyIdpsHint: Add an identity provider first, then create login connections for it.
ssoEmptyConnectionsHint: After adding a connection, employees can sign in with a corporate identity from the login page.
ssoPreviewHint: Generated from the currently enabled connections; the default sign-in starts authentication when the login page opens.
ssoPreviewCardSub: Choose your company identity system to sign in to {{name}}
ssoPreviewEmpty: With no enabled connection, the login page shows the AutoWonder account sign-in only.
ssoPreviewNote: The preview is not clickable; it only shows the login page entry. The real button reads “Sign in with {connection name}”.
ssoOverviewHint: SSO sign-in methods are maintained by platform administrators. You can view this overview only and cannot change the configuration.
ssoRegistrationHint: When off, the sign-up entry is hidden and public registration is rejected. Automatic account creation on first SSO sign-in is controlled per connection and unaffected by this switch.
ssoRegistrationUpdateFailed: Failed to save the registration setting
ssoDefaultLoginAria: Toggle the default sign-in state of {{name}}
ssoDefaultLoginHint: At most one default sign-in platform-wide; the login page starts it automatically. It cannot be set while the connection is disabled.
ssoDefaultLoginSet: Set as the only default sign-in entry
ssoDefaultLoginUpdateFailed: Failed to update the default sign-in setting
ssoAutoProvisionLabel: Create an account on first sign-in
ssoAutoProvisionHint: When an unbound identity is verified for the first time, create a passwordless normal account and bind it. No administrator or workspace access is granted. When off, no account is created; if same-username auto-binding is on, only a qualifying same-username account is bound, otherwise the user falls back to manual binding.
ssoUsernameClaimPlaceholder: Leave empty to follow the identity claim; or enter a custom claim such as login_name
ssoUsernameClaimHint: Defaults to the identity claim (SAML NameID or the configured subject attribute, OIDC sub); a custom claim overrides the default. The username is only used for first-time provisioning and same-username matching, and never replaces the SSO identity. Existing connections keep generated usernames while the field is empty.
ssoBindExistingLabel: Auto-bind accounts with the same username
ssoBindExistingHint: On the first SSO sign-in, a qualifying normal account with the same username can be bound and signed in automatically. If the account is already bound to another SSO identity or any other conflict exists, the user is told and binding stops without overwriting account data. When enabled, same-username users can bind without typing their existing AutoWonder password, so make sure the identity is stable, unique and never reassigned within the identity source. Administrators and other privileged accounts still need manual confirmation or binding.
ssoFeishuClaimHintActive: Active when the message channel is Feishu; leave empty to skip syncing. The value must be the Feishu user_id.
ssoFeishuClaimHintInactive: The current message channel is {{channel}}, so this mapping is inactive for now; the value is kept.
groupChatIdentityEditable: Configured; the application identity can still be changed.
groupChatNewIdentitySecretHint: Changing the application requires the new application's App Secret
groupChatNewIdentityTokenHint: Changing the application requires the new application's Verification Token
groupChatIdentityChangeTitle: The group-chat bot application identity will change
groupChatIdentityChangeImpact: Saving affects every shared group binding on this channel and terminates replies the old application has not sent yet. Add the new bot to the target groups first; real credential validity is reported by the live connection state after saving.

featureSwitches.saveFailed: Could not save the feature switch. Try again.
featureSwitches.readOnly: Only platform administrators may change feature switches.

duplicateIntent.title: Duplicate work item intent detection
duplicateIntent.toggle: Toggle duplicate work item intent detection
duplicateIntent.scopeHint: This switch applies to all workspaces and is off by default.
duplicateIntent.description: When enabled, after a work item is created or a changed title is saved the system silently checks the workspace for work items created in the last 30 days that share the same intent. Only matches send a system notification to the person who created or edited the work item. No match means no notification, and checks never delay create or save.
duplicateIntent.eligibility: Checks run only when the workspace Chief is configured and available. An unavailable Chief or a failed check ends silently, without prompts, waiting or recovery polling.
duplicateIntent.hint: Work item title matching compares titles with deterministic rules and needs no AI. It is always on and independent of this switch; an identical title after title entry opens a reminder you can ignore.
duplicateIntent.saveNow: This switch applies to all workspaces. It saves immediately on click; no separate save button is needed.
duplicateIntent.detect: After a work item is created or its edited title is saved, the system silently checks work items from the last 30 days in the same workspace for the same intent. Only when a possible duplicate is found is the operator notified; creation and saving are never affected.
duplicateIntent.chief: Whether the workspace Chief is configured and available is only checked when detection runs. If it is unavailable or the check fails, the flow ends silently with no prompt, waiting, or polling recovery. Enabling the switch does not pre-check Chief readiness.
duplicateIntent.titleRule: The exact-title rule is always enabled, does not use AI, and is unaffected by this switch; you can dismiss the reminder and continue.

registrationReview.title: User registration review
registrationReview.hint: When enabled, new self-service accounts need approval before sign-in. Turning it off leaves existing requests pending; new registrations become usable immediately.

workspaceCreationDefault.title: Allow workspace creation by default
workspaceCreationDefault.hint: When on, every user who can sign in may create workspaces. When off, regular users need an individual grant from a platform administrator.

mail.title: Email delivery settings
mail.hint: Supports SMTP passwords/app passwords and unauthenticated internal relays. Saved passwords are never displayed.
mail.securityStarttlsHint: Require an encryption upgrade; commonly port 587
mail.securitySslHint: Encrypted from connection start; commonly port 465
mail.securityNoneHint: Trusted internal relay only; no authentication credentials
mail.plainWarning: Notice: this connection is unencrypted. Use only for trusted internal relays authorized by source IP.
mail.passwordHint: Use provider-issued SMTP credentials, which may differ from your mailbox password. Leave the password blank to retain its saved value.
mail.testHint: Tests the current form settings; save them afterwards. Success means SMTP acceptance, not inbox delivery.
mail.invalid: Check the server, port, sender address, authentication account and test recipient
mail.verificationHint: When enabled, registration and profile email changes require verification. Codes expire in 10 minutes and can be resent after 60 seconds.
mail.verificationSaveFailed: Could not save. Make sure the current mail settings passed testing.
mail.suffixHint: When enabled, registration and email changes require an exact domain match.
mail.suffixPlaceholder: Enter a domain and press Enter to add
mail.forceHint: Notice: enabling this immediately blocks all unverified users, including the current administrator, from using the platform. Existing sessions, personal tokens and automations are restricted. Users must verify their email before continuing. System notifications will be sent.
mail.disableConfirmContent: This stops email verification, disables the existing-user requirement and removes email-verification restrictions. Re-enabling will not automatically require existing users to verify.
mail.forceConfirmContent: This takes effect immediately. All unverified users, including the current administrator, lose platform access. Existing sessions, personal tokens and automations are restricted until email verification. Unverified existing users will be notified.
mail.forceConfirmAlert: This affects every existing account. Confirm that affected users have been notified and the mail channel is working.

configurationDescription: Manage the platform brand and theme, message channels, feature switches, platform administrators, enterprise SSO and users.
imReadOnly: Only platform administrators can change message channels.
imSelectionLoadFailed: Failed to load the current channel
groupChatWarningAlert: The notification bot and the group-chat bot must use different application identities. Platform access status does not mean group bindings are usable, nor does it guarantee message handling or delivery.
switchChannelSameTarget: Choose the other channel; the current channel is unchanged.
groupChatDirtyHint: Unsaved group-chat draft; save the group-chat bot separately.
groupChatDraftHint: Takes effect only after saving the group-chat bot, separately from notification saving.
groupChatSecretMissingHint: AppSecret not configured; required when enabled. A new application requires a new Secret.
groupChatSecretConfiguredHint: AppSecret configured; leave blank to keep it. A new application requires a new Secret.
groupChatTokenMissingHint: Verification Token not configured; required when enabled. A new Feishu application requires a new Token.
groupChatTokenConfiguredHint: Verification Token configured; leave blank to keep it. A new Feishu application requires a new Token.
groupChatEncryptMissingHint: Encrypt Key not configured (optional). If provided, keep it consistent with the Feishu encryption policy.
groupChatEncryptConfiguredHint: Encrypt Key configured; leave blank to keep it. Keep it consistent with the Feishu encryption policy.
clearEncryptKeyHint: Also disable encryption on the Feishu side; takes effect only when saving the group-chat bot.
adminCandidatesFailed: Failed to load users available to add
adminResultUncertain: Addition not confirmed; user not found in the roster. Confirm again to retry
adminResultUnknown: Addition outcome unknown; read the roster again first
adminReconcileFailed: Roster reconciliation failed. Confirmation is locked; retry reading
notificationDraftHint: The toggle only edits the draft; it takes effect after you save the notification bot.
notificationDirtyHint: You have an unsaved draft; the toggle has not taken effect yet. Save the notification bot.
notificationSecretConfiguredHint: AppSecret is configured; leave it blank to keep the current value. A new application requires a new secret.
notificationSecretMissingHint: AppSecret is not configured; it is required when enabling. Credentials are not verified here.
